question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x) = \ln 7 + 7e^{x}$, find $f^{′}(x)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $ln⁡7$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

Using the addition rule, then, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡7+7{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(ln⁡7)+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7{e}^{x}) \\  & =0+7\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}) \\  & =7{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Given that $f(x)=5{e}^{x}+1$, find the slope of the tangent at $x=0.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The derivative of ${e}^{x}$ is just ${e}^{x}$ itself. On the other hand, $1$ is a constant, so its derivative is $0.$

$$

$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(5{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=0} \\  & =5{e}^{0} \\  & =5\cdot 1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
